newsitem.title: UK: LME copper steadier in sluggish inter-office trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper steadier in sluggish inter-office trade.

text.p: Copper prices nudged higher in inter-office trading on Friday but overall the base metals markets were stuck in the doldrums amid thin volumes, traders said.
A London Metal Exchange (LME) stock drawdown in aluminium failed to affect the price, underscoring the market's lack of interest.
"All the metal markets are settling in ranges. There has been no real news, no impetus to get things moving," a trader said. "Even the charts are not showing anything obvious."
In early trading three months copper crept higher to extend gains posted on late Thursday, which traders attributed to short covering out of the U.S.
It was last at $2,277 a tonne, up $17 from Thursday's kerb close.
But traders expected copper to run into stiff resistance around the top of the recent $2,245-$2,290 price range.
"It's going to take some volume to break through the $2,280-$2,295 level, and there hasn't been any volume recently," a trader said.
The market was watching the outcome a strike planned for Friday at Chile's major Escondida copper mine.
But management has said the planned stoppage was not expected to disrupt output.
Traders said the planned strike might be underpinning the market, but its effect was minimal.
Aluminum similarly shrugged off a stock drop of 3,650 tonnes, which brought the week's total declines to 12,375 tonnes.
Prices were last indicated at $1,552/54, compared to Thursday's kerb close of $1,550.
The market was consolidating but might eventually test the downside, with support around $1,550 towards the end of the day, some traders said.
Nickel prices edged back up above the $7,300 level, but analysts were still awaiting a confirmed break-out above important $7,500 resistance.
Prices were $45 firmer at $7,315.
Other base metal prices were also slightly firmer, without moving out of recent price bands.
Lead and zinc, which have repeatedly run into Far Eastern selling on the upside, were barely trading, traders said.
Both were $2 higher, at $636 and $1,245 respectively.
Tin was $25 higher at $5,710, and alloy was last indicated at $1,445/52, versus $1,440/45.
